summary:
Verifier pass on HEAD 863e5ea7 (sim and content unchanged since 09d330c0). I re-ran `node _harness/pacing.ts --seeds 10` and it reproduces line for line (RIFT adept mean 24.8, p90 27.1, PASS; _harness/_reports/closing_gameplay_verify_pacing10.txt). I re-ran the repo soak quick gate and it passes (_harness/_reports/fw_W4_soak_closing_gameplay_verify_quick.txt). I also wrote my own tool, _harness/_reports/closing_gameplay_verify_tools/v_gp.mts. It does not use the reviewer's (seed+slot+team) seating: each role's native is drawn by a seeded shuffle per seed, so teammates change from game to game. I ran 40 RIFT games (adept and veteran, seeds 301–320) and 40 mirrored veteran-vs-novice games (seeds 501–520). Summary: _harness/_reports/closing_gameplay_verify_summary.txt.

**CL-1 (major) is confirmed on independent lineups.**
- Credited takedowns by 10:00 are 1.90 (adept) and 1.75 (veteran) per game, and 2/20 and 5/20 games have none.
- Takedowns by 14:00 are 3.0 / 2.95.
- Fighter deaths per game by 5-minute bucket run 0.6 / 1.3 / 3.1 for the first 15 min, then 6.7 / 8.6.
- The median longest no-death stretch from 3:00 is 6.3–6.4 min.
- Shadehold kills before 14:00 are 0.35–0.45 per game.
- Dunsom, Ervet, Ardit, Ilsheta, Ulkro and Vashil first ult at a median 12–18 min.
- In the repo's own soak quick run, shadehold deaths by 15:00 are 0.1–0.4 per game and trade is 2–4 % of mode time.
- In one veteran game the first kill came at 13:00, after two Needles and a Lantern had already fallen.
The old 7.4–7.6 baseline recounts exactly from final_gameplay_verify_role_*.json. That baseline came from bots wandering and dying, so I judge against the gauge, not the old number. LoL's laning phase has kill pressure from level 2–3 and almost always a first blood before 10:00; on that gauge the gap is large.

**CL-2 is downgraded to minor.** The numbers reproduce:
- Sunsplinter's first take comes a median 8.7–8.8 min after spawn.
- Longshade is taken in 7/20 adept and 11/20 veteran games, and the taker wins 18/18.
But the Longshade-as-closer property is a recorded design decision under owner ruling 4 (_design/sections/modes_economy.md:358). It is mostly a selection effect: with the buff emptied, the taker still wins 36/50. The late Sunsplinter shares CL-1's root cause: the lane-phase gates at src/sim/bots/bot.ts:421-439 allow an objective only from the lane beside it, on an opening, and the jungler waits for an opening as well. A separate major would double-count CL-1. What remains is the open defender-answer follow-up, plus Splinters not stacking as §9 designs it (modes_economy.md:399 against the content/team_buffs.json comment).

**Minors.**
- CL-g1 reproduces exactly: veteran seed 8 ends at 13.2 min with 6 takedowns.
- CL-g2 is confirmed against VALE's own target. The shaftlight is level 6.2–6.3 at 10:00, and only 3/40 reach level 6 by 7:30, while modes_economy.md:50 says the duo road reaches level 6 at 7:00–8:00.
- CL-g3 is confirmed and slightly worse: veteran beats novice 31/40 on fresh seeds 501–520, so the two unseen windows together are 64/80 (80 %), under the 85 % done-bar. G3 moves to partly.
- CL-g4 and CL-g5 are confirmed from code and content.

One major is open, so the dimension is not on par. Score 6.

findings.title: RIFT bots barely fight before 15:00: the laning phase is quiet
findings.gauge: LoL's laning phase carries kill pressure from the level 2–3 spikes and early jungle ganks, and first blood almost always happens before 10:00. In high-elo solo queue, the reviewer's figure of roughly 6 kills per team by 10:00 matches my recollection of the Kaggle Diamond 10-min dataset (about 6.2), but neither of us verified it from the primary source this session. VALE's bots now produce about 2 kills by 10:00 in both teams combined, and about 10–25 % of games have none. The gap is large on any reasonable reading of the gauge.
findings.files: src/sim/bots/bot.ts (LANE_PHASE_END, lanePhase, selectMode :376-441), src/sim/bots/team.ts (thinkGank :571-590), src/sim/bots/micro.ts, src/sim/bots/difficulty.ts, _harness/probe_sim_bot_soak.ts
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced on lineups the reviewer did not use, and confirmed by the repo's own soak quick output. Severity stays major: the first 10–14 minutes of most bot-filled matches have almost no fights or ganks, and five or six fighters hold their ult until 12–18 min. A LoL player would notice that laning carries no kill threat.

findings.title: Objective contests are thin: Sunsplinter waits about 9 min, Longshade is taken late and only to close
findings.what:
The numbers are real, but the major framing does not hold up:
- **Longshade as the closer** is a recorded design decision (modes_economy.md:358, owner ruling 4: 'the signed-off numbers stay ... it is the game's closer'). It is mostly a selection effect: with the buff emptied, the taker still wins 36/50.
- **The Sunsplinter delay** comes from the same lane-phase gate as CL-1 (bot.ts:432-439: during laning an objective is taken only from the adjacent lane on an opening, and the jungler too waits for an opening). CL-1's fix addresses it, so a separate major double-counts it.
- **What remains** is the defenders' answer to an empowered Longshade wave, a follow-up named in §9 and not done, and Splinters, which the design says stacks to 3 (modes_economy.md:399) but which the sim and content only refresh (content/team_buffs.json $comment). That leaves Sunsplinter weak.
findings.gauge: LoL contests its early dragon-type objectives within a few minutes of spawn. The late boss is a strong but not certain closer; the reviewer's 80–88 % first-Baron figure is unverified. VALE's design accepts Longshade as a closer, which is not a gap by itself. The gaps are the uncontested first Sunsplinter, which is CL-1's root cause, and defenders who never answer an empowered wave.
findings.files: src/sim/bots/bot.ts (:432-439), src/sim/bots/team.ts (objective intent, defend), src/sim/core.ts (addTeamBuff stacking), content/team_buffs.json, _harness/probe_sim_bot_soak.ts
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced, but downgraded to minor. The Longshade-closer half is a documented design decision with its evidence on file. The Sunsplinter half is a symptom of CL-1's lane hold, so counting it again as a major double-counts one root cause. Splinters not stacking is a real design-to-sim drift the reviewer did not name.

findings.title: The lane hold can leave a base undefended: Hourbell lost at 13.2 min with 6 takedowns
findings.what: During the laning phase a bot defends only a dive on its own road or a base threat of 0.7 or more (bot.ts:421-426). Other roads keep laning while several enemies siege one road.
findings.evidence:
I reproduced it exactly:
```
node _harness/_reports/closing_gameplay_tools/cl_gp.mts --mode rift --seeds 1 --seed0 8 --mix veteran,veteran
```
Result: core at 13.2 min, 6 takedowns, team 0 loses 12 structures between 7.4 and 13.2 min (closing_gameplay_verify_vet8.json).
On my independent lineups no game ends before 16:00, but:
- veteran s301 ends at 17.5 min with 7 takedowns;
- veteran s302 loses two Needles and a Lantern before the first kill at 13:00.
Across 40 games, 7 have a structure fall before the first takedown, and 3 lose a Lantern before 14:00.
findings.gauge: In LoL, a base does not fall in the early game while its defenders are alive and home. Turret plates last until 14:00 and defenders rotate to sieges.
findings.fix: As the reviewer proposes: end the lane hold for a team that loses a structure or faces 3 or more sieging fighters, and gate that no RIFT core falls before 16:00.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced byte-for-byte. It is rare (1/20 in the reviewer's set, 0/40 core losses before 16:00 in mine), so minor is right. It shares CL-1's root cause.

findings.title: The duo road runs about 3 levels behind the solo laners; the carry reaches level 6 at about 9.5 min
findings.what: Even Wick XP sharing (src/sim/economy.ts:30, shareXp :156) leaves the shaftlight and lampglass about 3 levels behind the solo roads, which misses VALE's own design target.
findings.evidence:
closing_gameplay_verify_summary.txt, adept, levels by role:

| Time | Shaftlight | Lampglass | Solo laners |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5:00 | 3.8 | 4.0 | 5.8–5.9 |
| 10:00 | 6.3 | 6.5 | 9.0–9.2 |
| 20:00 | 9.8 | 10.1 | 13.2 |

At 7:30 the shaftlight averages 5.0–5.1, and only 3/40 shaftlights are level 6. _design/sections/modes_economy.md:50 targets level 6 for the duo road at about 7:00–8:00.
findings.gauge: In LoL the duo lane trails the solo lanes by roughly 1–2 levels at 10:00, and the carry has its ult in lane.
findings.fix: As the reviewer proposes, tune toward modes_economy.md:50 (level 6 at 7:00–8:00, at most 1.5 levels behind at 10:00). One option is a share bonus when two allies split a Wick's XP; another is a support-item XP pass. Keep it inside the probe_sim_rekey 10 % gate.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. It is stronger than the reviewer stated, because it misses VALE's own written target (modes_economy.md:50), not only the LoL gauge.

findings.title: Tier separation misses the 85 % bar on seed windows the tuning has not seen
findings.what: Veteran beats novice at about 80 % outside the tuned seed windows, against a done-bar of 85 %. The order is right and the gap is felt.
findings.evidence:
Two windows the tuning has not seen:
- seeds 101–120, the reviewer's: 33/40; I recounted it from closing_gameplay_mir_vn.json and nv.json;
- seeds 501–520, my run on independent lineups: 31/40 (closing_gameplay_verify_mir_vn.json and nv.json, v_gp.mts --mix veteran,novice and novice,veteran).
Combined that is 64/80 = 80 %.
findings.gauge: LoL's harder bot tiers reliably beat its easier ones (r09 §1.1).
findings.fix: Judge the tier gate on a rotating, untuned seed window with 40 or more games. Widen novice's macro and intent gaps in difficulty.ts if it still misses; do not change stats.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed and slightly worse on a second unseen window, so G3 moves to partly. It stays minor because the separation (about 80 %) is clearly felt.

findings.title: Per-fighter RIFT balance can't be measured: harness lineups lock teammates together
findings.what: pacing.ts and probe_sim_bot_soak.ts seat each role as natives[role][(seed + slot + team) % n]. With 3 natives in most roles, the same fighters always share a team, so their win rates are confounded.
findings.evidence: _harness/probe_sim_bot_soak.ts:155 (`pl[(seed + slot + team) % pl.length]`). For a 3-native role, slot 0 and slot 3 give the same index mod 3, and so do slot 1 and slot 4. No probe asserts RIFT per-fighter win bands.
findings.gauge: Riot keeps champions inside roughly a 45–55 % win band, which needs a balance read not confounded by teammates.
findings.fix: Add a balance suite with seeded per-role, per-team shuffles (as in closing_gameplay_verify_tools/v_gp.mts) over 200 or more games, reporting every fighter's win-rate confidence interval.

findings.title: Roster depth: three natives per role, so lane matchups keep recurring
findings.what: The 16 fighters split 3/3/4/3/3 across grovehunter, lampglass, dialcross, shaftlight and shadehold. That meets the draft gate but not r03's comfort target.
findings.gauge: LoL's large roster makes repeated lane matchups rare.
findings.fix: Short term, draft bots flex by secondaryRole. Long term, grow toward r03's 24-fighter comfort target.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed from content. It is a scope item, so minor is right.
